name: Sikadur-42 (au)
paste:
SIKADUR®-42 (AU): SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-42 (au), November 2021, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/3/sikadur_-42_au_.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-42 (au) where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2021, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur-42 (au) is a 3-component pourable solvent free grout based on epoxy resin and selected aggregates. Sikadur-42 (au) cures to form a hardened mortar with excellent adhesion to many substrates. Sikadur- 42 (au) ease of application makes it ideally suited to high performance grouting in critical site applications.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur -42(au) has been developed for use in building and civil engineering applications such as:
    - Crane rails
    - Machine bedding and baseplates
    - Holding down bolts
    - Starter bars
    - Cavity filling
    - Bridge bearing pads
    - Precast grouting

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-42 (au)
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: High strength pourable epoxy resin grout
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (November 2021, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Compressive strength (p.1).
    - BS 6319: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Tensile strength (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Insensitive to moisture during application, cure or whilst in service
    - Applicable at low temperatures down to 5°C.
    - High early strength
    - Excellent adhesion to a wide variety of dry and damp substrates such as concrete, stone, fibrous cement, synthetic resins, wood and most metals.
    - High tensile and flexural strength, vibration resistant.
    - Supplied in factory proportioned units
    - Easy to use
    - Unaffected by wide range of chemicals
    - Good flow characteristics even in thin layers
    - Proven track record
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Three Component Epoxy Grout
    - Density: Approx. 2.0 kg per/lt (2000 kg/1000 lt)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Tensile strength: ~8 MPa @ 7 days (BS 6319)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | 1 Day | 7 Day |
    | ~50 MPa | ~70 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS1478.2:2005)
    Note printed: 50mm x 50mm cube
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 14.6kg kit (~7.3lt)
    - Shelf life: ~24 months from date of manufacture
    - Storage conditions: Store under dry conditions in out of direct sunlight.(minimum 5°C - maximum 35°C)

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2021, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. Mortar and concrete must be older than 28 days (dependent on minimum strength requirements). Verify the substrate strength (concrete, natural stone etc.). The substrate surface (all types) must be clean, dry and free from contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, existing surface treatments and coatings etc. Steel substrates must be de-rusted to a standard equivalent to Sa 2.5. The substrate must be sound and all loose particles must be removed. Substrate must be dry or mat damp and free from any standing water, ice etc.
3.3 Substrate preparation - Concrete, mortar, stone. Substrates must be sound, dry, clean and free from laitance, ice, standing water, grease, oils, old surface treatments or coatings and all loose or friable particles must be removed to achieve a laitance and contaminant free, open textured surface.
3.4 Substrate preparation - Steel.
    - Must be cleaned and prepared thoroughly to an acceptable quality standard equivalent to SA 2.5 i.e. by blastcleaning and vacuum. Avoid dew point conditions. Surface and base plate contact area must be clean and sound. For best results, the substrate shall be dry. Remove dust, laitance, oils, grease, curing compounds, impregnations, waxes, foreign particles, coatings, and disintegrated materials by mechanical means, i.e. chipping with a chisel, blastcleaning etc. All anchor pockets or sleeves must be free of water. Apply grout immediately to prevent re-oxidizing / rust formation.
    - For optimum results: When grouting areas or equipment that is sensitive to vibration, it is recommended that the contact surfaces are prepared according to the latest edition of the American Petroleum Institute’s Recommended Practice 686 “Machinery Installation and Installation Design”, Chapter

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2021, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: A : B : C= 2 : 1 : 14 by weight
    - Yield: approx. 7.3 lt for 14.6kg kit
    - Curing time: 7 days full cure @ 23oC
4.3 Layer thickness. Generally, suitable thickness depends on clearance, distance of flow, ambient and substrate temperatures and pour size. Range of application typically 10 mm - 60 mm. For deeper applications Sikadur 42 HP should be used.
4.4 Pot Life.
    | Temperature - 14.6 kg kit | Time |
    | ~20oC | 65 mins |
    | ~35oC | 35 mins |
4.5 Mixing.
    - Mix components A and B in the component A pail for approx. 30–60 seconds with a paddle attached to a low speed drill (300–450 rpm). Avoid aeration while mixing until the material becomes uniformly blended in colour and viscosity. Place the mixed epoxy into an appropriate mixing vessel. Slowly add the contents of component C (to keep air entrapment at a minimum) dependent on flow requirements (observe the correct mixing ratio) and mix until uniform and homogeneous (approx. 3 min).
    - Mix only that quantity which can be used within its potlife. Never mix Component A and B without adding component C (as the exothermic reaction between A and B alone generates excess heat) Leave Sikadur®-42 (au) to stand in the normal mixing vessel for 2 – 3 minutes until the majority of entrained air bubbles have dispersed
4.6 Application method / tools.
    - The consistency of the Sikadur®-42 (au) epoxy grout system requires the use of permanent or temporary forms to contain the material around base plates, for example. In order to prevent leakage or seepage, all of these formers must be sealed. Apply polyethylene film or wax to all forms to prevent adhesion of the grout. Prepare the formwork to maintain more than 100 mm liquid head to facilitate placement. A grout box equipped with an inclined trough attached to the form will enhance the grout flow and minimize air encapsulation.
    - Pour the mixed grout into the prepared forms from one or two sides only, to eliminate air entrapment. Maintain the liquid head to ensure intimate contact to the base plate. Place sufficient epoxy grout in the forms to rise slightly above the underside (3 mm) of the base plate. The minimum void depth beneath the baseplate shall be 10 mm. Where the void beneath the base plate is greater than 60 mm, place the epoxy grout in successive 60 mm lifts or less, once the preceding lift has cooled. Once hardened check the adhesion by tapping with a hammer.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment.
    - Sweep excess grout into appropriate containers for disposal before it has hardened.
    - Dispose of in accordance with applicable local regulations. Uncured material can be removed with Sika Colma Cleaner. Cured material can only be removed mechanically.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (November 2021, Version 01.02) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: 1 Day | 7 Day; ~50 MPa | ~70 MPa (AS1478.2:2005)
    - Tensile strength: ~8 MPa @ 7 days (BS 6319)
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-42 (au), November 2021, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/3/sikadur_-42_au_.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur 42 (au) Part B, version 12/10/2021, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/Sikadur%2042(au)%20Part%20B%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur 42 (AU) Part A, version 01/07/2024, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/MSDS%20Sikadur-42%20(AU)%20Part%20A%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-42 (au) Part B, version 09/08/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sds-sikadur-42-aupartb.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Material Safety Data Sheet containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
